scenes.say: If a pod crashes, who brings it back? Let's talk about Deployments and why they're the backbone of Kubernetes workloads.

scenes.label: Deployment
scenes.sub: Manages identical pods, handles updates and rollbacks.
scenes.say: A Deployment manages a group of identical pods for you. It keeps the right number running, and takes care of updates or rollbacks when needed.
Here's how it flows: the Deployment defines what you want, the ReplicaSet makes sure you have enough pods, and the pods actually run your app.

scenes.title: Deployment Commands
scenes.say: You can scale up with a single command, update your app image, check rollout progress, or roll back if something breaks. Super handy for real-world ops.

scenes.question: If you delete a pod, is it gone for good?
scenes.wrong: Yes, you have to recreate it manually.
scenes.right: Nope! The ReplicaSet spins up a new pod automatically.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: if you delete a pod, Kubernetes doesn't just let it go. The ReplicaSet will create a new one to match your Deployment's desired state.
